top.title: Microsoft: Hackers in China, N Korea using ARTEX AI tool to break into global tech systems
top.description: Chinese and North Korean state-sponsored hacking crews are among the growing number of groups known for using the ARTEX pentesting tool in attacks, Microsoft said this week. ARTEX is an open source, AI-powered penetration testing framework that attackers have adopted to automate reconnaissance, credential attacks, and exploitation since its public release in July. Campaigns that have been linked to ARTEX have targeted cloud environments, IT software like ConnectWise , and financial institutions globally, sometimes reaching privileged access in under three hours. Salt Typhoon is arguably the most recognizable name on the list of ARTEX beneficiaries – the group responsible for attacks on telcos AT&T and Verizon , US government systems , UK prime minister's aides , and more. The lesser-known Crystal Typhoon – the group behind the ArcaneDoor attacks back when Microsoft called it Storm-1849 – was also named alongside it, as were North Korea's Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet. Microsoft also named China-state-aligned Storm-0940, linked to the ConnectWise compromise, and financially motivated, Cambodia-based Storm-3358. It had previously reported both groups' use of ARTEX. Chinese cybersecurity company ThreatBook claimed ownership of ARTEX in November. GitHub user "Autumn-27" originally published its source code with a Chinese-language interface in July. Various forks of the repo, which was taken down in October, have meant that the same framework is available in multiple languages. According to Infrawatch , there are more than 130 variants of ARTEX in circulation, and it is the most widely used agentic offensive framework (AOF) at present. Like other offensive security tools adopted by criminals, ARTEX can lower the effort required to mount attacks. Experienced groups can also use it to automate repetitive work and pursue multiple avenues at once. As Microsoft echoed this week, after the FBI and AWS issued their warnings earlier this month , ARTEX is proving to be a useful tool for the more sophisticated groups to streamline and hasten their attacks too. It's being used to help attackers steal AI and cloud credentials at "industrial scale," as AWS put it, which provide attackers access to advanced models for free. Microsoft says ARTEX can progress from reconnaissance to persistent, privileged access within minutes, depending on its configuration and the target's defenses. "In the past few weeks, we've reported several distinct campaigns that abused ARTEX to search public repositories for exposed secrets, enable supply chain compromise, and scan internet-facing systems for exploitation," its threat intelligence team blogged . "These campaigns illustrate how threat actors use ARTEX to automate various stages of the attack chain. top.description: Sep 27, 2020; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk (11) runs the ball against New York Giants defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence (97) during the first quarter of a NFL football game at MetLife Stadium. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect For the remainder of the season, Brandon Aiyuk has joined the Washington Commanders practice squad. ESPN ‘s Adam Schefter reported the deal on Wednesday. The 28-year-old wide receiver agreed to a one-year contract after clearing waivers. This move ends his time with the San Francisco 49ers and starts a new chapter in Washington. The signing reunites Aiyuk with quarterback Jayden Daniels, his former teammate from Arizona State. They played together during the 2019 college season. Aiyuk enters the league with a chance to rebuild his career after a two-year absence from game action. His last on-field performance came in 2024 before a knee injury cut his season short. A Fresh Start in Washington The Commanders needed help at the wide receiver position. Star player Terry McLaurin landed on injured reserve, leaving the group thin on depth. Washington now adds Aiyuk to a corps that includes Stefon Diggs, Antonio Williams, and Treylon Burks. The team sits at 4-5-1 on the season, just two games back of the New York Giants for the NFC East lead. Aiyuk brings a proven track record to the roster. Since joining the league in 2020, he has tallied 294 catches, 4,305 yards, and 25 touchdowns. His career-best came in 2023 when he posted 1,342 receiving yards. That performance earned him a second-team All-Pro selection. Before the 2024 season began, he secured a four-year extension valued at up to $120 million with the 49ers. His time in San Francisco ended poorly after the injury. Aiyuk tore his ACL, MCL, and meniscus on Oct. 20, 2024. He missed the entire 2025 season while rehabbing the knee. Conflicting reports surfaced about his health during that long recovery. The distance between player and team grew as the 49ers voided contract guarantees for the 2025 season. Leadership Views on Work Ethic Washington general manager Adam Peters knows Aiyuk well. Peters worked with the receiver in San Francisco from 2020 to 2023. He spoke highly of Aiyuk during a weekly appearance on 106.7 The Fan on Wednesday. Peters called him a “smart football player” and said he was among the 49ers’ “hardest workers on the team”. “One of the things that I don’t think anyone can dispute is his work ethic,” Peters said. He added that this drive is how Aiyuk became an All-Pro-type player. Peters pointed to the 2023 season as proof of his on-field talent. He noted that Aiyuk was a true No. 1 receiver at that time. “He was a true No. 1 receiver at the time. He’s a guy who’s a tough cover, he’s great after the catch. top.title: UNICEF, NGE, DAME others make case for 18.3m out-of-school children
top.description: By Chioma Obinna & Juliet Umeh Media leaders, government officials and development partners have called for urgent action to address Nigeria’s child welfare and education challenges, raising concern over the 18.3 million out-of-school children in the country. They warned that poverty, insecurity, displacement, poor learning conditions and inadequate investment in maternal and child healthcare were undermining the survival, development and future of millions of Nigerian children. The stakeholders spoke at the 2026 World Children’s Day High-Level Media Symposium in Lagos, organised by UNICEF Nigeria in partnership with the Nigerian Guild of Editors, NGE, and the Diamond Awards for Media Excellence, DAME. In his opening address, President of the NGE, Mr Eze Anaba, challenged government, media organisations, community leaders and the private sector to take responsibility for the growing number of children without access to education. Citing a UNICEF report that put the number of out-of-school children at 18.3 million, Anaba said: “It’s our collective responsibility to ask why. “In a country of about 200 and something million people and 18 million plus of that population is on the streets, not going to school. It’s not only alarming. It’s a collective responsibility.” He questioned whether stakeholders were doing enough to address the crisis, asking: “Have we reminded government? Community leaders, have they done their part? Has the media done enough? The private sector, has it done enough?” Anaba also raised concerns over the location of some public schools close to bus stops, motor parks and train stations, warning that such environments could expose children to negative influences at a critical stage of their development. He said children’s welfare must not be treated as an annual talking point without measurable commitments. “It is not enough for us to be episodic. Every year we come and remind ourselves that look, we have to build a future for the kids. Last year, on this same programme, I made a commitment on behalf of my newspaper that Vanguard would do more. Have we done enough?” he asked. He called for an action plan spelling out what government, media organisations, businesses and other stakeholders would do to improve children’s lives. Speaking, UNICEF representative in Nigeria, Wafaa Saeed, called for sustained investment in children, particularly during the first 1,000 days of life, warning that neglect during this period could have lifelong consequences. “You cannot pause a baby’s brain development while waiting for economic recovery. From conception to age two, 80 percent of human brain growth occurs, making investment in the first 1,000 days critical to a child’s survival, development and future,” Saeed said. top.title: Trinity Rodman breaks her silence after breakup with Ben Shelton
top.description: Jan 22, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Trinity Rodman of the Washington Spirit wipes a tear during a press conference at BMO Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images One of America’s young power couples has officially called things off, with USWNT star Trinity Rodman and tennis star Ben Shelton reportedly agreeing to go their separate ways after two years together, according to the Daily Mail. Per the outlet, the couple, who began dating around March 2025 and were frequently seen at one another’s sporting events each other, found that long distance and their intesse work schecules made things difficult on their relationship. Rodman, the daughter of NBA legend Dennis Rodman, was a constant presence in Shelton’s box throughout the US Open in September, and she even jetted straight from a game in Washingotn to make it to New York for Shelton’s match in teh final, and was captured cryinginside Arthur Ashe Stadium in the wake of her boyfriend’s loss to Alexander Zverev. Shelton spoke on the difficulties that their schedules presented for their relationship in September. “It is really difficult,” he told US Weekly. “I think what a lot of people don’t see is when we actually do have time or a couple of days off, we’re so exhausted that it’s tough to do anything. It is tough to make time.” “Sometimes I leave these tournaments and I’m a bit of a zombie,” he added. “I’m not the most fun person to be around. But we make a lot of sacrifices for our sport. I’d say both of us are chasing things for our sport. We’re not where we want to be yet, we’re not in our primes. So this is kind of crunch time. “This is going to be the hardest, most grueling time in our relationship, from my perspective. None of it is easy. But being able to have someone to lean on who’s such an elite athlete and doing things at a really high level as well, it helps in so many ways.” “Reset time” On Wednesday, Rodman made her first public comments since news of the split broke via her Instagram story, writing, “Trust the process. Reset time.” Four hours later, Shelton made a post of his own, although his vibes were a lot different, captioning his post with a emoji and added the “Life is Good” remix as the background track. Shelton lost to to Carlos Alcaraz in the semifinal of the ATP Finals in Turin, Italy, on Saturday, but it appears he’s feeling good about where he’s at in life now that he’s single. She also suffered a shoulder injury within the first few minutes of the final which will cause her to miss the upcoming CONCACAF W Championship tournament for the USWNT. Her time 0ff may be a blessing in disguise, as it’ll allow her the personal time she needs to reflect and reset. top.title: Charles Leclerc ‘hurt’ by accusations of disloyalty after recent spats with Lewis Hamilton
top.description: Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton downplayed tensions ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix after a series of costly and dramatic on-track spats between the Ferrari pair. Leclerc said there was no clause in his new contract giving him number one status at the team, quelling speculation on that topic, and said he was “hurt” by accusations made towards him of disloyalty to Ferrari. The teammates clashed during the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday three weeks on from a high-profile incident in Mexico , prompting Hamilton to urge the Scuderia to clarify their policy on team orders. Speaking ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix, Leclerc said: “The only thing that I don't like seeing is people questioning my integrity to the team, my ⁠love for the team. I've been in Ferrari since ​2019. ⁠I think there's nothing clearer than the love I have for the team, and I will do absolutely everything in order to bring Ferrari back to the top. “Of course, mistakes happen along the way and always will. We just try to minimise them, and particularly between teammates. “I think it's more the question mark that I have seen going around that hurts me more than anything else.” The Monegasque said he was not allowed to discuss possible solutions to the track situation or any rules of engagement - “I cannot disclose that” - but acknowledged the need for a solution. He said: “At the end of the day, we are two very strong drivers that want to finish one ahead of the other. “Unfortunately, it finished recently, whether it's in (Las Vegas) or Monza or Mexico, there's been a bit too many events of those lately, ⁠and we need to find a solution as a team to make sure that these kinds of things don't happen again. “As a team, we cannot afford to clash between teammates, and I think that is very clear for everyone. For the clash in particular of Las Vegas, as I said, I took responsibility. “I think there's just tension around that we just need to dissipate and make sure that we look at more positive days in the future. That's all I'm looking for.” Hamilton was tight-lipped on whether any agreement had been found ahead of the final two races of the season, saying: “We had internal discussions. Everything stays internal. “It's been positive. Charles and I sat here earlier and had a good discussion.” Ferrari are second to champions Mercedes in ‌the constructors’ standings with two races remaining and ​should secure that place in Qatar.

top.title: 7 Years Later, Hollywood’s Most Notorious Fantasy Flop Deserves Another Shot
top.description: I vividly remember learning the phrase “uncanny valley” in 2019. First came the trailer for Sonic the Hedgehog that April, with those alarmingly human teeth. Then came the first trailer for Tom Hooper’s Cats in July. Suddenly, there was a name for a feeling I’d had my whole life. The uncanny valley is that uneasy feeling you get when something looks or moves almost like a real person, but some small detail makes the whole thing feel wrong. That feeling is a lot more common these days, now that AI-generated videos are everywhere. But it was Cats that really brought the uncanny valley into the popular lexicon.

top.description: Carlos Augusto: “I want to keep giving my all for Inter” A story that began in 2023 is set for more exciting chapters. To mark his contract extension with Inter until 2031, Carlos Augusto spoke exclusively to Inter TV: Carlos Augusto and Inter together until 2031. How much does this contract extension mean to you? “I’m very happy and grateful for the faith shown in me. I hope to repay the Club on the pitch, as I always have. I hope to keep improving and help Inter stay at the top, winning as much as possible.” You joined Inter at 24 and have since won two Serie A titles, the Coppa Italia and the Supercoppa. What first comes to mind when you look back on what you’ve achieved in Nerazzurri colours so far? “The truth is that time has flown by. In my first season, we earned our second star and it was a special time. When I arrived, I knew the aim was to compete for trophies, and we need to keep doing that. I want to honour the shirt and win as much as possible.” What does wearing the Inter shirt every day mean to you? “It’s an honour to wear this shirt. Inter is one of the best clubs in the world, and I always try to give my all on the pitch to win matches and honour the Nerazzurri shirt.” Game by game, you’ve become a key figure in the team. How do you see the coming years at Inter? “First of all, I need to thank my teammates. They’re the reason I’m able to improve. I’m with them every day, and I’ve been here for a few seasons now. I hope to keep helping Inter stay at the top, because team honours always come before individual ones.” What message do you have for the Inter fans? “I want to thank the fans, who always stand by me. I hope to keep giving my all, stay here for as long as possible and help the team win.”

top.title: Archie Brown could solve Man United’s biggest headache without Ineos blowing their £50m winter kitty
top.description: Archie Brown could solve Man United’s biggest headache without Ineos blowing their £50m winter kitty Not signing a left-back has come back to bite Manchester United. An injury to the club’s only natural left-back, Luke Shaw , has forced them to rely on makeshift options, several of whom have struggled badly. The position has become the Red Devils’ clearest weakness. Last week United chief executive Omar Berrada told Sky Sports : “It’s widely reported we looked for reinforcement in the left-back position… could we have signed an additional defender? Yes, but we have to find the right players at the right value. There’s no point spending £40–50m on players we don’t think improve the team.” As the winter transfer window approaches, United are therefore expected to stick to that transfer principle: They will not sign just any left-back; they want someone who genuinely improves the side. Archie Brown could be that player. The Fenerbahçe left-back has long been linked with Old Trafford, yet United have never acted on their interest. Tempting Archie Brown release clause A golden opportunity has now arisen. German transfer journalist Florian Plettenberg reports that Brown has a €23 million (£19 million) release clause that can be triggered this winter, and the 24-year-old is keen on a move to the Premier League. Man United must seize Archie Brown transfer opportunity United reportedly have a £50 million winter budget, with a striker also viewed as a crucial signing for Mauricio Pochettino. If Ineos are wise and want a successful winter transfer window, they must pounce on Brown. He is athletic, bombs forward down the left flank and thrives in high-tempo football without needing time to adapt to physical duels – ideal for Pochettino’s style. He offers progressive carries, crosses and goals while contributing clearances, interceptions and tackles, making him one of the most complete left-backs available. Securing a player of Brown’s quality for £19 million would be daylight robbery. It would strengthen a major weakness while still leaving room to address other areas, like the attack, as Pochettino fights to keep United in the Premier League.

top.title: Rafael Nadal now explains his famous quote about Nick Kyrgios’ potential in 2019
top.description: “If, If, if… Doesn’t exist.” Those were the words of 22-time Grand Slam champion Rafael Nadal in a press conference after beating Nick Kyrgios in the second round of Wimbledon in 2019, when asked what the then-24-year-old Australian would be capable of achieving if he were to adopt a more professional approach to his tennis career. Nadal had just emerged victorious in their thrilling four-set match at the All England Club, having lost to Kyrgios at the Mexican Open earlier that year. His quote about his opponent that day has since become famous, and he recently expanded on it, two years after retiring from tennis. Photo by Visionhaus/Getty Images Rafael Nadal recalls his comments about Nick Kyrgios Relayed his words back to him in an interview with Brut , Nadal said: “But that’s the truth in the end. I mean, I always heard since I was a kid, if this guy wanted to practice more… so, do it. So that’s the truth, you know. “I think everybody can hide behind an if, you know. And at the end of the day, for me, ‘if’ is a word that is nothing. You did what you did; that’s it, as simple as that. And that’s, yeah, in some way, that’s the way that I understand life. “And that’s the way that I understand my career, you know. Because when I lost because I got injured or when I was not able to play Grand Slam, [people] said, if I was able to play… But I was not able to play. So it’s over. “It doesn’t matter. I lost because I had a problem on my knee. Okay. But I lost. At the end of the day, the result is I lost. It doesn’t matter if it’s because I had or I don’t have. At the end, it’s about results, and that’s the reality. Then it’s always trying to find excuses to find a way to protect yourself.” Photo by Andy Cheung/Getty Images Rafael Nadal’s head-to-head record against Nick Kyrgios Not many players in tennis history can say they beat Nadal once, let alone three times, a tally Kyrgios managed to record. Kyrgios beat Nadal in their first ever clash on the ATP Tour at the 2014 edition of the Wimbledon championships. Aged 19 at the time, wildcard Kyrgios overcame Nadal in four sets to reach the quarterfinals of the grass-court major. Kyrgios became the first man outside the top 100 to beat a world number one at a Grand Slam since 1992. Kyrgios’ second win over Nadal came at the 2017 Cincinnati Open, where he beat him in straight sets to advance to the semifinals of the ATP Masters 1000 event. He bagged his last victory over Nadal in Acapulco in 2019, coming back from a set down to win and make it 3-3 in their head-to-head. The head-to-head ultimately finished 6-3 in favour of Nadal, who won their last three meetings. They were supposed to play for a 10th time in the 2022 Wimbledon semifinals, but Nadal withdrew due to injury.

top.title: The Garmin Forerunner 265S is down to $300, its best price of the year
top.description: The Forerunner 265S is great for runners with small wrists. | Photo by Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge The Forerunner 265S may not be the newest or flashiest Garmin, but it’s one that I’ve always loved most in testing. For runners with smaller wrists, it fits nicely. The battery life is pretty good thanks in part to its OLED touchscreen. When I reviewed it a few years ago, I called it the Goldilocks of fitness watches at the time, and the only thing that bugged me was its price. But now that it’s down to $299.99 (a $150 discount off its MSRP) at Amazon and Best Buy for Black Friday, I can easily recommend it. Garmin Forerunner 265S (42mm) Garmin’s Forerunner 265S is identical to the standard 265, only it features a slightly better battery life and a smaller 42mm build for those with more petite wrists. Where to Buy: $449.99 $299.99 at Amazon $449.99 $299.99 at Best Buy The neat thing about Garmins in general is that you really don’t need the latest models to get the most out of the company’s platform. Its watches tend to get firmware updates for several years after launch, which is how long the average Garmin user tends to hold on to theirs. This particular watch is best suited for folks who want something a bit slimmer and smaller, enjoy a pop of color, and want a little extra fitness tracking prowess — but don’t need the whole kit and caboodle that sends the price up by hundreds. There are a few other Garmin models I like that are also on sale during Black Friday. I wish that I had 10 arms to fully vet every single last one, but alas. That said, here are some others that I have tested and recommend: The Garmin Fenix 8 is $749 at Amazon , Best Buy , and REI , which is a 25 percent discount off its original price. Its higher price comes down to having more features than the Forerunner 265S, so it’s really best for someone who does multiple outdoor sports and could make use of its handy LED flashlight. Garmin’s Venu 4 is $449 at Amazon , Best Buy , and REI , an 18 percent discount. This is a great option if you’re looking for more of a smartwatch that does fitness than a fitness-y watch that looks like a smartwatch. It’s a fine line, but if you know, you know. Finally, Garmin’s Forerunner 970 is $100 off, costing $649 at Amazon , Best Buy , and REI . This is what I’d recommend to marathoners who need something a bit more robust but not as heavy-duty as the flagship Fenix line. I’ve used it to train for a few races and it’s a solid upper-midrange (for Garmin!) option.

top.description: By Henry Ojelu The United Kingdom and the Mirabel Centre have renewed calls for stronger protection, sustained support and access to justice for survivors of sexual and gender-based violence in Nigeria. top.title: Boxing chiefs to assess Fury mental health before fight
top.description: Tyson Fury revealed his schizophrenia diagnosis in a new Netflix documentary [Getty Images] The British Boxing Board of Control is looking into Tyson Fury's comments about his schizophrenia diagnosis but is "fairly confident" the British heavyweight will be cleared to fight Anthony Joshua next month. Fury, 38, is due to face Joshua at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on 11 December, with the ringwalk expected in the early hours of 12 December. In a Netflix documentary out on Friday, he says he heard voices threatening him and his family in the months after he beat Wladimir Klitschko to become world champion in 2015. "We are in the process of dealing with the matter but if there are any medical issues we wouldn't let anyone box, doesn't matter if it's Tyson Fury or not, it could be anybody," Robert Smith, the board's general secretary, told BBC Sport. "I'm fairly confident he will be absolutely fine. We're dealing with it now and we'll have an answer very shortly." Under regulation 8.1(b) of the British Boxing Board of Control's 2026 rules and regulations , schizophrenia is among the conditions that "may preclude" a boxer from obtaining a first licence, while for an existing licence holder the board "may take such action as in its absolute discretion it sees fit". Smith would not say what the process would involve over the next few days, saying "it's a medical matter". He said that all boxers on the card will undergo medical checks, adding: "If our doctors are satisfied he's fit to box, he will box." In the documentary, Fury and his wife Paris recall his admission to hospital in June 2016 with a suspected heart attack. Doctors said he had suffered an anxiety attack. He was diagnosed with schizophrenia after he left hospital, according to the film. The NHS describes schizophrenia as a form of psychosis, and symptoms can include hallucinations, delusions and muddled thoughts and speech. "Words can't explain the darkness I was in," Fury says. The heavyweight, who struggled with drug and alcohol addiction after beating Klitschko, says a Halloween night out in 2017 prompted him to return to training, calling that a "turning point" after being "embarrassed by how I looked". He went on to beat Deontay Wilder in 2020 to become world heavyweight champion for a second time. nigeria.description: By Chioma Obinna & Juliet Umeh Media leaders, government officials and development partners have called for urgent action to address Nigeria’s child welfare and education challenges, raising concern over the 18.3 million out-of-school children in the country. They warned that poverty, insecurity, displacement, poor learning conditions and inadequate investment in maternal and child healthcare were undermining the survival, development and future of millions of Nigerian children. The stakeholders spoke at the 2026 World Children’s Day High-Level Media Symposium in Lagos, organised by UNICEF Nigeria in partnership with the Nigerian Guild of Editors, NGE, and the Diamond Awards for Media Excellence, DAME. In his opening address, President of the NGE, Mr Eze Anaba, challenged government, media organisations, community leaders and the private sector to take responsibility for the growing number of children without access to education. Citing a UNICEF report that put the number of out-of-school children at 18.3 million, Anaba said: “It’s our collective responsibility to ask why. “In a country of about 200 and something million people and 18 million plus of that population is on the streets, not going to school. It’s not only alarming. It’s a collective responsibility.” He questioned whether stakeholders were doing enough to address the crisis, asking: “Have we reminded government? Community leaders, have they done their part? Has the media done enough? The private sector, has it done enough?” Anaba also raised concerns over the location of some public schools close to bus stops, motor parks and train stations, warning that such environments could expose children to negative influences at a critical stage of their development. He said children’s welfare must not be treated as an annual talking point without measurable commitments. “It is not enough for us to be episodic. Every year we come and remind ourselves that look, we have to build a future for the kids. Last year, on this same programme, I made a commitment on behalf of my newspaper that Vanguard would do more. Have we done enough?” he asked. He called for an action plan spelling out what government, media organisations, businesses and other stakeholders would do to improve children’s lives. Speaking, UNICEF representative in Nigeria, Wafaa Saeed, called for sustained investment in children, particularly during the first 1,000 days of life, warning that neglect during this period could have lifelong consequences. “You cannot pause a baby’s brain development while waiting for economic recovery. nigeria.title: NDC using ‘rig and die’ slogan to mobilise for mass rigging – Keyamo
nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo SAN, has accused the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC of using the “rig and die” slogan as a cover to mobilise its members and “rig the elections massively.” Keyamo made the claim on Thursday in a post on his X account. He was reacting to a clarification of the slogan by the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi. “There is no need for Peter Obi to clarify the ‘rig and die’ slogan and do damage control. We know what it means. The slogan is nothing but a subterfuge for them to mobilise themselves and rig the elections massively as they did in a part of the country in 2023 but still failed”, he said. The minister asked what would stop a party that is “sufficiently armed to play the role of law-enforcement agents” from rigging elections itself. “If a party in a contest with other parties is sufficiently armed to play the role of law-enforcement agents, what stops that same party from rigging the elections itself? Are they saints?” he asked. He argued that no party can be both contestant and referee. “You cannot be a participant in a contest, yet you want to act as the umpire under the guise that you don’t trust the umpire! That is creating a graver absurdity than the one you’re trying to solve!” he said. The slogan became a national talking point after a former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, the NDC candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District, used it at a campaign event in Uvwie, Delta State, in October. “Anybody who rigs the election on that day, we will kill him!” Omo-Agege said, adding: “It is rig and die.” Tension over the slogan grew after gunmen attacked Omo-Agege’s campaign team at Uduere, in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, this Monday. His media adviser, Sunny Areh, said four people were killed and four others critically injured, while Omo-Agege was unhurt. Other reports put the death toll at six. Keyamo condemned the killings the same day. nigeria.title: Lawal reaffirms refusal to negotiate with bandits
nigeria.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, has reiterated his administration’s decision not to negotiate with bandits terrorising the state, insisting that efforts would instead focus on reclaiming ungoverned areas and restoring security. Lawal stated this on Thursday at the graduation ceremony of the Zamfara Forest Guards held at Government Secondary School, Gada Biyu, Gusau. More than 1,000 forest guards graduated after undergoing training in weapons handling, physical fitness, combat readiness, civil-military relations, security cooperation, community engagement and the rule of law. The armed forest guard initiative was launched by President Bola Tinubu on May 24, 2025, to train residents to secure forests and other ungoverned areas across the country. At the ceremony, Lawal expressed appreciation to Tinubu and the National Security Adviser for the Federal Government’s support for the initiative. He also commended security agencies, the training coordinator and instructors for their roles in preparing the guards for service. Addressing the graduates and their families, the governor said Zamfara needed to reclaim its vast ungoverned areas, which he said had become hideouts for bandits and other criminal groups. “We must urgently reclaim Zamfara’s vast ungoverned areas, which have become safe havens for bandits, criminals and terrorists. “This will require sustained cooperation between federal and state authorities, a reliable security presence and the restoration of public services. “Our goal is to ensure displaced families can return safely, and communities can farm, trade and rebuild their livelihoods,” he said. The governor said his administration had invested substantially in security agencies over the past three years through the provision of operational equipment, vehicles, surveillance technology and logistical support. He listed the equipment provided to security agencies as more than 30 Armoured Personnel Carriers, 200 operational pick-up vehicles, 20 Toyota Buffalo vehicles and over 1,000 specialised motorcycles. He added that additional vehicles and motorcycles had also been supplied to the Homegrown Community Protection Guards. On surveillance, Lawal said the state had acquired drones, including an 80-metre endurance model capable of covering up to 50 kilometres and operating continuously for eight hours. According to him, the equipment would improve reconnaissance, situational awareness and coordination in difficult terrain. nigeria.title: Mock Accreditation: INEC Faces Crucial Test As 100 Million Voters Await 2027 Elections
nigeria.description: With exactly 50 days before Nigerians return to the ballot, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is preparing for a nationwide test that could offer an important indication of whether the country is ready for another fiercely contested general election. On Saturday, November 28, the electoral umpire will deploy its Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and electronic results upload technology across 17,676 selected polling units in a mock exercise designed to identify operational weaknesses, test equipment reliability and strengthen public confidence ahead of the 2027 elections. The exercise, scheduled for 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., will cover two polling units in each of the country’s 8,838 registration areas, giving INEC an opportunity to assess the performance of its electoral technology across different locations before the presidential and National Assembly elections on January 16, 2027, and the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections on February 6. #OsunDecides2026: Election Officers Take Delivery Of Materials, Mobilise To Polling Units during the Osun State governorship election on August 15, 2026. It comes against the backdrop of lingering controversies surrounding the 2023 general elections, particularly the failure to upload presidential election results to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) in real time, technical difficulties associated with BVAS and allegations of electoral irregularities. Chairman of INEC, Joash Amupitan, described the mock exercise as an important part of preparations for the forthcoming elections, while urging Nigerians to participate. The commission’s Director of Voter Education and Publicity, Victoria Meci, explained that the exercise would allow INEC to establish the effectiveness and reliability of its equipment before election day. “We don’t want to wait till the elections before we test the ruggedness, readiness and functionality of the system,” she said during an appearance on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily . According to her, the commission has reduced the accreditation threshold to 850 voters per BVAS device, with additional machines to be provided at polling units with larger voter populations. The exercise will also test the electronic upload of results to IReV, although Meci acknowledged that successful transmission would depend on network availability. 100 Million Voters, 176,846 Polling Units The scale of the preparations reflects the size of Nigeria’s electorate. INEC says it is now managing a verified national register of more than 100 million voters after removing over 1.6 million invalid, duplicated, and deceased records from the previous register of approximately 103 million. nigeria.description: Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, has denied allegations linking him, the All Progressives Congress (APC), or its supporters to the alleged violent attack on members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during the party’s activities in Benin City, the state capital. Speaking at the APC presidential campaign rally in Ehor, headquarters of Uhunmwonde Local Government Area, and Ekpoma in Esan West, the governor described the allegations as unfounded, insisting that neither the state government nor the APC had any reason to disrupt opposition political activities. ﻿ Okpebholo alleged that the incident involved irresponsible elements who were fighting among themselves, dismissing claims of government involvement. He said his priority remained the development of Edo State, stressing that he would not divert his attention to political violence or activities capable of undermining the progress of the state. The governor recalled that he did not engage thugs during his senatorial and governorship campaigns, alleging that a police officer was killed during the governorship election by individuals he claimed were linked to the opposition. He also vowed to sustain his administration’s crackdown on cultism and other criminal activities, insisting that elections should be conducted based on the principle of one man, one vote. Okpebholo urged residents to participate actively in the electoral process, while thanking APC supporters for their turnout at the rally. Earlier, Deputy Governor Dennis Idahosa urged the people to vote for APC candidates across all levels in the 2027 general elections, while party chairman Jarrett Tenebe commended the governor’s efforts in tackling kidnapping and cultism, urging continued support for President Bola Tinubu and other APC candidates. Political thugs on Wednesday attacked the campaign convoy and campaign office of the NDC in Benin City, after the party said it received an intelligence report on a possible attack at its town hall meeting in Benin, where its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, was expected to address supporters. The Edo State Coordinator of the party’s campaign council, John Yakubu, said the party had been informed of plans to disrupt the event, as members prepared to leave their campaign office to receive Obi at the airport. Videos obtained by our correspondent showed blood stains on the party convoys, including bullet casings seen on the floor of the party’s campaign office. business.title: Bitcoin Has Become Boring, Finally
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Has Become Boring, Finally The 2019 Lightning conference in Berlin was lit: five hundred “cypherpunks” getting each other high on visions of a future with peer-to-peer electronic cash. Attending a bitcoin conference back in the day felt like being a teenager at a friend’s party while their parents were out of town. It was exciting and new. The feeling was the opposite of FOMO: something big was happening, we were on the inside, and the rest of the world was going to envy us. It was the kind of party that you could only have when the adults weren’t looking. Whenever someone bought a beer (with bitcoin), everyone would hoot and holler and record it on their phones for Instagram/Twitter (it was still called Twitter). Lightning was the bleeding edge. We called it “the Lightning Network” (capitalized, if you please), and talking about it felt like talking about string theory: something so far out you’re not even sure it’s real. I spent a lot of time invoking the abacus . Those are the times some of us remember fondly and keep trying to relive at bitcoin conferences today. That’s why we engage in rituals like drone shows, Satoshi Rockamoto sets, beefsteak dinners , and video game tournaments for sats, but it’s not the same. The ratio of bitcoin OG speakers to suits is shifting. Many event rooms are half empty, and the halls and meeting rooms are full of people negotiating cap tables and profit-sharing splits. The adults haven’t shut the party down, but they have crashed it, and it kinda feels like their party now. The most exciting thing I noticed at the last bitcoin conference I attended was that nothing exciting happened. And that’s worth celebrating. From Tech Subcultures to Mainstream Tech Adoption The road to boring is seldom smooth. Technological innovation benefits from passion and bold ideas. People work harder on a project when they feel strongly about it and identify closely with like-minded collaborators. That’s where tech subcultures, their rituals, and their dogmas come from. But such passion and tribalism feed conflict, at least for a while until the tech goes mainstream, and normies, who couldn’t care less about subculture squabbles, take over. This progression from an exciting new technology that inspires strong emotions to a humdrum utility is not unusual. World-changing innovations often (always?) start with a committed subculture that identifies fiercely with their weird tech before the mainstream adopts it and soon expects it. In fact, this trajectory has become the standard doctrine of tech marketing. entertainment.title: M.Inc PR Joins Industry Stakeholders to Explore Africa’s Credit Economy at ACE 2026
entertainment.description: A cross section of industry leaders and stakeholders during the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo 2026 held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. These conversations connected access to credit with the need for individuals to understand financial management, borrowing and long-term wealth creation. This focus reflects the February 2026 memorandum of understanding between CreditRegistry and the University of Lagos, through its Entrepreneurship and Skills Development Centre (ESDC), to integrate the Africa Consumer Credit Academy (ACCA) curriculum into the Centre’s programmes. The initiative is intended to strengthen financial literacy through learning opportunities, mentorship, certification and engagement with industry. entertainment.title: As Nigeria Rethinks Teacher Education, Tunji Olowolafe Makes a Case for Better-Prepared Educators
entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. For Dr. Olowolafe, the commitment to educators is also deeply personal. His mother was a teacher, his elder sister taught for years at Baptist Academy, Lagos, and his late wife, Gbemisola Olowolafe, was a lifelong educator. The actor was just as memorable away from the screen, where his sharp wit, outspoken nature and candid opinions made him a fascinating personality in interviews. For generations of Nollywood viewers, Pete Edochie was the actor they could recognise before he had even finished his first sentence. He became one of Nigerian cinema’s most familiar faces, often playing kings, chiefs, fathers and respected elders. entertainment.title: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Passes Away at 79
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). entertainment.description: For many people, buying property is one of the biggest financial decisions they will ever make. Yet, knowing who to trust, how to verify ownership and whether a property is worth the investment can make the process overwhelming. It is a challenge Solape Fayemi hopes to address with the launch of Saina Properties , a real estate company now operating across Nigeria, the United Kingdom, the United States and the United Arab Emirates. Officially unveiled at an event held on 17 November at the Marriott Hotel, Ikeja GRA, Lagos, Saina Properties is built around a simple idea: property ownership should be guided by sound advice, proper verification and professional support, not just the excitement of closing a deal. For Solape, whose experience in the investment industry shaped her understanding of money, risk and wealth creation, the decision to establish the company came from recognising the need for a more considered approach to real estate. “We are not building Saina Properties because the world needs another company selling properties. We are building Saina because we believe there is room for a different kind of real estate experience. One where advice comes before the transaction, where due diligence is not treated as an inconvenience, and where people are encouraged to ask questions, understand their options and make informed decisions,” she said at the launch. That philosophy is reflected in the company’s three core areas of expertise: Advisory & Verification, Sales & Brokerage, and Developments . Rather than focusing solely on connecting buyers to properties, Saina brings together the guidance investors need to assess opportunities, the support required to navigate property transactions, and involvement in real estate development. The company is also building on experience gained before its official launch, having supported more than 25 clients with property opportunities across different markets. An important part of its proposition is the role of professional expertise in protecting property investors. Fayemi’s position raises a familiar question: people consult doctors for medical concerns and lawyers for legal matters, so why do some investors leave significant property decisions in the hands of relatives simply because they are available or familiar with the location? The 28-year-old wide receiver agreed to a one-year contract after clearing waivers. This move ends his time with the San Francisco 49ers and starts a new chapter in Washington. The signing reunites Aiyuk with quarterback Jayden Daniels, his former teammate from Arizona State. They played together during the 2019 college season. Aiyuk enters the league with a chance to rebuild his career after a two-year absence from game action. His last on-field performance came in 2024 before a knee injury cut his season short. sports.title: Charles Leclerc ‘hurt’ by accusations of disloyalty after recent spats with Lewis Hamilton
sports.description: Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton downplayed tensions ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix after a series of costly and dramatic on-track spats between the Ferrari pair. Leclerc said there was no clause in his new contract giving him number one status at the team, quelling speculation on that topic, and said he was “hurt” by accusations made towards him of disloyalty to Ferrari. The teammates clashed during the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday three weeks on from a high-profile incident in Mexico , prompting Hamilton to urge the Scuderia to clarify their policy on team orders. Speaking ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix, Leclerc said: “The only thing that I don't like seeing is people questioning my integrity to the team, my ⁠love for the team. I've been in Ferrari since ​2019. ⁠I think there's nothing clearer than the love I have for the team, and I will do absolutely everything in order to bring Ferrari back to the top. “Of course, mistakes happen along the way and always will. We just try to minimise them, and particularly between teammates. “I think it's more the question mark that I have seen going around that hurts me more than anything else.” The Monegasque said he was not allowed to discuss possible solutions to the track situation or any rules of engagement - “I cannot disclose that” - but acknowledged the need for a solution. He said: “At the end of the day, we are two very strong drivers that want to finish one ahead of the other. “Unfortunately, it finished recently, whether it's in (Las Vegas) or Monza or Mexico, there's been a bit too many events of those lately, ⁠and we need to find a solution as a team to make sure that these kinds of things don't happen again. “As a team, we cannot afford to clash between teammates, and I think that is very clear for everyone. For the clash in particular of Las Vegas, as I said, I took responsibility. “I think there's just tension around that we just need to dissipate and make sure that we look at more positive days in the future. That's all I'm looking for.” Hamilton was tight-lipped on whether any agreement had been found ahead of the final two races of the season, saying: “We had internal discussions. Everything stays internal. “It's been positive. Charles and I sat here earlier and had a good discussion.” Ferrari are second to champions Mercedes in ‌the constructors’ standings with two races remaining and ​should secure that place in Qatar.

sports.title: Archie Brown could solve Man United’s biggest headache without Ineos blowing their £50m winter kitty
sports.description: Archie Brown could solve Man United’s biggest headache without Ineos blowing their £50m winter kitty Not signing a left-back has come back to bite Manchester United. An injury to the club’s only natural left-back, Luke Shaw , has forced them to rely on makeshift options, several of whom have struggled badly. The position has become the Red Devils’ clearest weakness. Last week United chief executive Omar Berrada told Sky Sports : “It’s widely reported we looked for reinforcement in the left-back position… could we have signed an additional defender? Yes, but we have to find the right players at the right value. There’s no point spending £40–50m on players we don’t think improve the team.” As the winter transfer window approaches, United are therefore expected to stick to that transfer principle: They will not sign just any left-back; they want someone who genuinely improves the side. Archie Brown could be that player. The Fenerbahçe left-back has long been linked with Old Trafford, yet United have never acted on their interest. Tempting Archie Brown release clause A golden opportunity has now arisen. German transfer journalist Florian Plettenberg reports that Brown has a €23 million (£19 million) release clause that can be triggered this winter, and the 24-year-old is keen on a move to the Premier League. Man United must seize Archie Brown transfer opportunity United reportedly have a £50 million winter budget, with a striker also viewed as a crucial signing for Mauricio Pochettino. If Ineos are wise and want a successful winter transfer window, they must pounce on Brown. He is athletic, bombs forward down the left flank and thrives in high-tempo football without needing time to adapt to physical duels – ideal for Pochettino’s style. He offers progressive carries, crosses and goals while contributing clearances, interceptions and tackles, making him one of the most complete left-backs available. Securing a player of Brown’s quality for £19 million would be daylight robbery. It would strengthen a major weakness while still leaving room to address other areas, like the attack, as Pochettino fights to keep United in the Premier League.

sports.title: Rafael Nadal now explains his famous quote about Nick Kyrgios’ potential in 2019
sports.description: “If, If, if… Doesn’t exist.” Those were the words of 22-time Grand Slam champion Rafael Nadal in a press conference after beating Nick Kyrgios in the second round of Wimbledon in 2019, when asked what the then-24-year-old Australian would be capable of achieving if he were to adopt a more professional approach to his tennis career. Nadal had just emerged victorious in their thrilling four-set match at the All England Club, having lost to Kyrgios at the Mexican Open earlier that year. His quote about his opponent that day has since become famous, and he recently expanded on it, two years after retiring from tennis. Photo by Visionhaus/Getty Images Rafael Nadal recalls his comments about Nick Kyrgios Relayed his words back to him in an interview with Brut , Nadal said: “But that’s the truth in the end. I mean, I always heard since I was a kid, if this guy wanted to practice more… so, do it. So that’s the truth, you know. “I think everybody can hide behind an if, you know. And at the end of the day, for me, ‘if’ is a word that is nothing. You did what you did; that’s it, as simple as that. And that’s, yeah, in some way, that’s the way that I understand life. “And that’s the way that I understand my career, you know. Because when I lost because I got injured or when I was not able to play Grand Slam, [people] said, if I was able to play… But I was not able to play. So it’s over. “It doesn’t matter. I lost because I had a problem on my knee. Okay. But I lost. At the end of the day, the result is I lost. It doesn’t matter if it’s because I had or I don’t have. At the end, it’s about results, and that’s the reality. Then it’s always trying to find excuses to find a way to protect yourself.” Photo by Andy Cheung/Getty Images Rafael Nadal’s head-to-head record against Nick Kyrgios Not many players in tennis history can say they beat Nadal once, let alone three times, a tally Kyrgios managed to record. Kyrgios beat Nadal in their first ever clash on the ATP Tour at the 2014 edition of the Wimbledon championships. Aged 19 at the time, wildcard Kyrgios overcame Nadal in four sets to reach the quarterfinals of the grass-court major. Kyrgios became the first man outside the top 100 to beat a world number one at a Grand Slam since 1992. Kyrgios’ second win over Nadal came at the 2017 Cincinnati Open, where he beat him in straight sets to advance to the semifinals of the ATP Masters 1000 event. He bagged his last victory over Nadal in Acapulco in 2019, coming back from a set down to win and make it 3-3 in their head-to-head. The head-to-head ultimately finished 6-3 in favour of Nadal, who won their last three meetings. They were supposed to play for a 10th time in the 2022 Wimbledon semifinals, but Nadal withdrew due to injury.

But, if you do find some time between playing backyard football and scarfing down some turkey (like many of us are currently indulging in), you should check out what we’re feeling thankful for this year! Once again, happy, happy Thanksgiving! Enjoy! Zac Penson Thankful for: The Ryan Family I could talk about the season Northwestern football started to have under David Braun and Chip Kelly, but after the disaster that the team has become after losing Aidan Chiles, the memory fans will take from this season is the one artifact that will stand as a colosseum on campus for decades to come: the new stadium. The incredible generosity from the Ryan Family is something that myself and ‘Cats fans (as well as probably the away fans that tend to fill our stadium) alike will take away from this season in the long run. It is just an absolutely beautiful stadium that will hopefully lead Northwestern down a path of successful recruitment and cement its place as a legitimate football contender in the Big Ten. If it weren’t for the generosity of the Ryan Family and specifically the effort Pat Ryan Jr. put into the stadium, we wouldn’t have the incredible new Wildcat Wall, the over the top lounges, incredible sight lines, open concourses, the Great Chicago Food Festival, Thunderstruck… the list could go on forever. For all of that, thank you, and Happy Thanksgiving ‘Cats fans! Donovan West Thankful for: Northwestern field hockey I’m not going to lie and say I’m the biggest Northwestern field hockey fan who watched every game this season. There are other diehards on Inside NU that have you covered in that aspect. However, I’m still thankful for our three-time national championship-winning ‘Cats. Not only because they have brought so much pride and glory to Evanston over the past couple of years, but also, selfishly, because it’s a good conversation starter at the Thanksgiving table. When my family asks about NU’s sports, or lack thereof, I run through the typical lowlights of men’s and women’s basketball as well as the head-spinning football and tragedy of Aiden Chiles, but am able to end with, “But hey, the field hockey team just won the National Championship.” So, I’m thankful for the ‘Cats for saving my Thanksgiving conversations. sports.title: Boxing chiefs to assess Fury mental health before fight
sports.description: Tyson Fury revealed his schizophrenia diagnosis in a new Netflix documentary [Getty Images] The British Boxing Board of Control is looking into Tyson Fury's comments about his schizophrenia diagnosis but is "fairly confident" the British heavyweight will be cleared to fight Anthony Joshua next month. Fury, 38, is due to face Joshua at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on 11 December, with the ringwalk expected in the early hours of 12 December. In a Netflix documentary out on Friday, he says he heard voices threatening him and his family in the months after he beat Wladimir Klitschko to become world champion in 2015. "We are in the process of dealing with the matter but if there are any medical issues we wouldn't let anyone box, doesn't matter if it's Tyson Fury or not, it could be anybody," Robert Smith, the board's general secretary, told BBC Sport. "I'm fairly confident he will be absolutely fine. We're dealing with it now and we'll have an answer very shortly." Under regulation 8.1(b) of the British Boxing Board of Control's 2026 rules and regulations , schizophrenia is among the conditions that "may preclude" a boxer from obtaining a first licence, while for an existing licence holder the board "may take such action as in its absolute discretion it sees fit". Smith would not say what the process would involve over the next few days, saying "it's a medical matter". He said that all boxers on the card will undergo medical checks, adding: "If our doctors are satisfied he's fit to box, he will box." In the documentary, Fury and his wife Paris recall his admission to hospital in June 2016 with a suspected heart attack. Doctors said he had suffered an anxiety attack. He was diagnosed with schizophrenia after he left hospital, according to the film. The NHS describes schizophrenia as a form of psychosis, and symptoms can include hallucinations, delusions and muddled thoughts and speech. "Words can't explain the darkness I was in," Fury says. The heavyweight, who struggled with drug and alcohol addiction after beating Klitschko, says a Halloween night out in 2017 prompted him to return to training, calling that a "turning point" after being "embarrassed by how I looked". He went on to beat Deontay Wilder in 2020 to become world heavyweight champion for a second time. sports.title: Former Real Madrid star heaps praise on Arda Guler: ‘Sees the game before everyone else’
sports.description: Former Real Madrid star heaps praise on Arda Guler: ‘Sees the game before everyone else’ Former Real Madrid star Jorge Lopez Marco, better known as Tote, believes Arda Guler has become an enormously important figure in the team’s attacking play. Speaking on Radio MARCA , the 48-year-old former attacking midfielder highlighted the Turkish international’s exceptional reading of the game and ability to create opportunities for others as qualities that set him apart. Tote’s praise for Guler Tote’s praise for Guler comes after the 21-year-old midfielder signed a new long-term contract with Real Madrid until 2032 . The playmaker has grown into a vital cog in the team’s attacking unit under Jose Mourinho this season, and his form has been key to the team’s ten-game winning run in all competitions. He has already racked up four goals and nine assists from 16 appearances across all competitions for the Spanish capital giants. A key player for Real Madrid. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) And Tote believes that Guler’s vision sets him apart, allowing Real Madrid to create advantages in the final third and produce a different kind of attacking football when possession goes through him. “He’s the one who sees the game before everyone else,” he said. The former attacker, who spent time at Real Madrid between 1997 and 2001, pointed to Guler’s ability to identify passing opportunities early, provide the final ball and make the team’s attacking movements more effective. Concerns about Real Madrid’s contrasting displays However, Tote also highlighted the contrast between Real Madrid’s performances in different periods of matches, pointing at their performance in the first half and second half during the 5-1 win over PSV. “If another team catches you, you’ll probably go into halftime 0-3 down,” he warned. Tote (R) warned Real Madrid about their slow sart. (Photo by Nuno Correia. Credit: Allsport UK/Allsport) However, he was encouraged by the response after the break as Real Madrid showed greater intensity, moved the ball with more urgency and created more opportunities. The 48-year-old now-retired star also pointed to Kylian Mbappe and Thibaut Courtois as two players who keep making the difference for Los Blancos . “With a goalkeeper and a striker like Real Madrid has, they’re going to fight for everything,” he stated. When asked to name his favourites for the Champions League, Tote suggested that it was too early in the campaign and that the real test will arrive in March and April. “That’s when you see the teams with personality, when you see the winners and those who don’t hesitate.” he explained.

sports.title: Raiders QB Fernando Mendoza thankful for Aaron Rodgers on Thanksgiving
sports.description: Somewhere in the middle of airing his grievances with the Pittsburgh Steelers on Wednesday, Aaron Rodgers took a moment to say something nice about a fellow quarterback. Imagine Fernando Mendoza’s surprise to find out it was him. Rodgers was on “The Pat McAfee Show” explaining how things had gone sideways with Steelers coach Mike McCarthy when he got around to the Denver film. Pittsburgh plays the Broncos on Friday. The Raiders had just been through Denver on Sunday, which is how a rookie making his second NFL start earned a cameo in somebody else’s very public breakup. Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza (15) throws against the Denver Broncos during an NFL football game in Denver, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. AP Photo/Jack Dempsey “And I’ll tell you: Hey, the kid Mendoza, man. He was running around, making some plays in the scramble.” Funny thing about that tape. If Rodgers goes back to the third quarter and watches what Mendoza did before throwing a 19-yard touchdown pass to tight end Ian Thomas, he might recognize the move the young quarterback busted out. After all, Mendoza borrowed it from Rodgers. The Raiders call it the guitar fake. Watch Mendoza’s hands as running back Ashton Jeanty approached Mendoza as if he was going to be handed the ball. The empty hand carries out the handoff while the other keeps the football tucked against his body. FERNANDO MENDOZA TO IAN THOMAS pic.twitter.com/05xuiDSy3b — wok (@wokdior) November 22, 2026 Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers gestures at a news conference after an NFL football game in Philadelphia, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. AP Photo/Chris Szagola For a beat, the quarterback looks like a guy playing air guitar. By the time Mendoza brings the ball back into view, Thomas is wide open. The extra point tied a game the Raiders once trailed 17-0. It makes sense that any young quarterback would pick out elements of a future Hall of Famer like Rodgers and make them their own. Even more so in the case of Mendoza, who played his first two seasons at Cal, Rodgers’ alma mater. “Yeah, Aaron Rodgers, he also went to Cal, so it’s a little funny, but it was something that we’ve worked on a lot,” Mendoza said. Mendoza spent his last college season at Indiana working primarily from the shotgun, several yards behind the center, with the defense in front of him and the back alongside him. Get under center in Klint Kubiak’s offense, and the view changes in a hurry. Mendoza has to take the snap, turn his back on the defense, meet a runner coming downhill, then get his head around and find his receiver. His feet have to sell the handoff, too. “So, if you don’t have a lot of experience detailing under center handoffs, it’s sometimes hard to then develop the fakes,” Mendoza said. technology.title: Microsoft: Hackers in China, N Korea using ARTEX AI tool to break into global tech systems
technology.description: Chinese and North Korean state-sponsored hacking crews are among the growing number of groups known for using the ARTEX pentesting tool in attacks, Microsoft said this week. ARTEX is an open source, AI-powered penetration testing framework that attackers have adopted to automate reconnaissance, credential attacks, and exploitation since its public release in July. Campaigns that have been linked to ARTEX have targeted cloud environments, IT software like ConnectWise , and financial institutions globally, sometimes reaching privileged access in under three hours. Salt Typhoon is arguably the most recognizable name on the list of ARTEX beneficiaries – the group responsible for attacks on telcos AT&T and Verizon , US government systems , UK prime minister's aides , and more. The lesser-known Crystal Typhoon – the group behind the ArcaneDoor attacks back when Microsoft called it Storm-1849 – was also named alongside it, as were North Korea's Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet. Microsoft also named China-state-aligned Storm-0940, linked to the ConnectWise compromise, and financially motivated, Cambodia-based Storm-3358. It had previously reported both groups' use of ARTEX. Chinese cybersecurity company ThreatBook claimed ownership of ARTEX in November. GitHub user "Autumn-27" originally published its source code with a Chinese-language interface in July. Various forks of the repo, which was taken down in October, have meant that the same framework is available in multiple languages. According to Infrawatch , there are more than 130 variants of ARTEX in circulation, and it is the most widely used agentic offensive framework (AOF) at present. Like other offensive security tools adopted by criminals, ARTEX can lower the effort required to mount attacks. Experienced groups can also use it to automate repetitive work and pursue multiple avenues at once. As Microsoft echoed this week, after the FBI and AWS issued their warnings earlier this month , ARTEX is proving to be a useful tool for the more sophisticated groups to streamline and hasten their attacks too. It's being used to help attackers steal AI and cloud credentials at "industrial scale," as AWS put it, which provide attackers access to advanced models for free. Microsoft says ARTEX can progress from reconnaissance to persistent, privileged access within minutes, depending on its configuration and the target's defenses. "In the past few weeks, we've reported several distinct campaigns that abused ARTEX to search public repositories for exposed secrets, enable supply chain compromise, and scan internet-facing systems for exploitation," its threat intelligence team blogged . "These campaigns illustrate how threat actors use ARTEX to automate various stages of the attack chain. technology.title: Tech's outage problem needs maintenance, not conspiracy theories
technology.description: Years of technical debt, increasingly complex systems, and underinvestment in IT operations have left organizations vulnerable to major outages, according to Forrester. The analyst pointed to a seven-day stretch in November when failures disrupted Microsoft 365, US air traffic control, banking, and other critical services. The coinciding outages provoked "a slew of conspiracy theories about cyberattacks and AI," Forrester said. "The real culprit is tragically mundane: the culmination of decades of technical debt, the frenetic buildout of massively complex and highly interdependent systems, the concentration of risk, and the underinvestment in advanced operations." Forrester urged technology suppliers and in-house IT teams to prioritize resilience as their systems grow more complex. Otherwise, "the tech estate will collapse like a house of cards, taking down consumer and business trust with it." Earlier this month, Microsoft was left struggling to restore many of its cloud services after a core process running on some servers became "overwhelmed" and its attempts to fix the problem failed. Some of its services did not recover for another 24 hours. In October, Google Cloud blamed a "power event" for taking down multiple online products for customers in Western Europe. Affected services included BigQuery Data Transfer Service, Cloud Filestore, Cloud Run, Google App Engine, and Google Kubernetes Engine. In October last year , a major outage impacted Amazon Web Services (AWS), with even Amazon's own web page reported to be offline and dozens of other online services and websites affected. Aviation and banking were also hit this month. A communications outage triggered a nationwide ground stop in the US on November 13 , while incidents involving JPMorgan Chase, United Airlines, Apple, Workday, Gmail, and other services added to the sense of widespread instability. "Claims that these were all part of one connected cyberattack or conspiracy are highly unlikely. The real story is much more mundane," the report said . Forrester argued that organizations have prioritized visible improvements over repairs to the underlying technology. "Modernization investments have favored visible change over structural renewal," wrote report authors Lauren Nelson and Mark Moccia. "Organizations routinely fund new customer experiences, cloud migrations, platform consolidation, and AI initiatives because leaders can connect them to growth or productivity. "They are less enthusiastic about updating core systems, simplifying architectures, retiring obsolete components, and eliminating fragile interfaces. The result is a modern front end resting on an aging, brittle, and increasingly interconnected estate." Forrester's recommendations are to map dependencies, test failures and recovery under realistic conditions, and use incidents and near misses to identify weaknesses before they cause another outage. ®
